arxiv-1706-03793.title: A “problem of time” in the multiplicative scheme for the n n -site hopper
arxiv-1706-03793.creator: Fay Dowker, Vojtěch Havlíček, Cyprian Lewandowski, Henry Wilkes
arxiv-1706-03793.description: Abstract Quantum Measure Theory (QMT) is an approach to quantum mechanics, based on the path integral, in which quantum theory is conceived of as a generalised stochastic process. One of the postulates of QMT is that events with zero quantum measure do not occur, however this is not sufficient to give a full picture of the quantum world.

arxiv-1808-02892.title: A Game of Surface Codes: Large-Scale Quantum Computing with Lattice Surgery
arxiv-1808-02892.description: Abstract Given a quantum gate circuit, how does one execute it in a fault-tolerant architecture with as little overhead as possible? In this paper, we discuss strategies for surface-code quantum computing on small, intermediate and large scales. They are strategies for space-time trade-offs, going from slow computations using few qubits to fast computations using many qubits.

arxiv-2310-19563.title: Data-driven optimal control via linear programming: boundedness guarantees
arxiv-2310-19563.creator: Lucia Falconi, Andrea Martinelli, John Lygeros
arxiv-2310-19563.description: Abstract The linear programming (LP) approach is, together with value iteration and policy iteration, one of the three fundamental methods to solve optimal control problems in a dynamic programming setting. Despite its simple formulation, versatility, and predisposition to be employed in model-free settings, the LP approach has not enjoyed the same popularity as the other methods.

arxiv-2401-17689.title: Constraining black hole parameters with the precessing jet nozzle of M87*
arxiv-2401-17689.creator: Shao-Wen Wei 1,2 , Yuan-Chuan Zou 3 , Yu-Peng Zhang 1,2 , Yu-Xiao Liu 1,2
arxiv-2401-17689.description: Abstract Recently, Cui et al. [Nature 621 , 711 (2023)] reported that the jet nozzle of M87* exhibits a precession with a period of approximately 11 years. This finding strongly suggests that the supermassive black hole in the core of M87 galaxy is a spinning black hole with a tilted accretion disk.

arxiv-2406-16766.title: Conformal time series decomposition with component-wise exchangeability
arxiv-2406-16766.creator: Derck W. E. Prinzhorn, Thijmen Nijdam, Putri A. van der Linden, Alexander Timans
arxiv-2406-16766.description: Abstract Conformal prediction offers a practical framework for distribution-free uncertainty quantification, providing finite-sample coverage guarantees under relatively mild assumptions on data exchangeability. However, these assumptions cease to hold for time series due to their temporally correlated nature. In this work, we present a novel use of conformal prediction for time series forecasting that incorporates time series decomposition.

arxiv-2412-18042.title: Time-Probability Dependent Knowledge Extraction in IoT-enabled Smart Building
arxiv-2412-18042.creator: Hangli Ge, Hirotsugu Seike, Noboru Koshizuka
arxiv-2412-18042.description: Abstract Smart buildings incorporate various emerging Internet of Things (IoT) applications for comprehensive management of energy efficiency, human comfort, automation, and security. However, the development of a knowledge extraction framework is fundamental. Currently, there is a lack of a unified and practical framework for modeling heterogeneous sensor data within buildings.

arxiv-2510-03917.title: Transductive and Learning-Augmented Online Regression
arxiv-2510-03917.creator: Vinod Raman, Shenghao Xie, Samson Zhou
arxiv-2510-03917.description: Abstract Motivated by the predictable nature of real-life in data streams, we study online regression when the learner has access to predictions about future examples. In the extreme case, called transductive online learning, the sequence of examples is revealed to the learner before the game begins.

arxiv-2511-03945.title: Direct Semantic Communication Between Large Language Models via Vector Translation
arxiv-2511-03945.creator: Fu-Chun, Yang, Jason Eshraghian
arxiv-2511-03945.description: Abstract In multi-agent settings, such as debate, reflection, or tool-calling, large language models (LLMs) pass messages as plain tokens, discarding most latent semantics. This constrains information transfer and adds unnecessary computational overhead. We form a latent bridge via vector translations, which use learned mappings that enable direct semantic exchange between representation spaces.

arxiv-2511-17085.title: Why Do Language Model Agents Whistleblow?
arxiv-2511-17085.creator: Kushal Agrawal, Frank Xiao, Guido Bergman, Asa Cooper Stickland
arxiv-2511-17085.description: Abstract The deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) as tool-using agents causes their alignment training to manifest in new ways. Recent work finds that language models can use tools in ways that contradict the interests or explicit instructions of the user.

arxiv-2601-22474.title: Unrewarded Exploration in Large Language Models Reveals Latent Learning from Psychology
arxiv-2601-22474.creator: Jian Xiong, Jingbo Zhou, Zihan Zhou, Yixiong Xiao, Le Zhang, Jingyong Ye, Rui Qian, Yang Zhou, Dejing Dou
arxiv-2601-22474.description: Abstract Latent learning, classically theorized by Tolman, shows that biological agents (e.g., rats) can acquire internal representations of their environment without rewards, enabling rapid adaptation once rewards are introduced. In contrast, from a cognitive science perspective, reward learning remains overly dependent on external feedback, limiting flexibility and generalization.

plos-pone-0004929.description: PLOS ONE research article. Trophic structure, or the distribution of biomass among producers and consumers, determines key ecosystem values, such as the abundance of infectious, harvestable or conservation target species, and the storage and cycling of carbon and nutrients. pmc-11366253.title: Utility of Common Bile Duct Identification on Biliary Ultrasound in Emergency Department Patients
pmc-11366253.creator: Christopher Thom, Justin Yaworsky, Kevin Livingstone, David Han, Jakob Ottenhoff
pmc-11366253.description: BackgroundBiliary ultrasound is often utilized in the evaluation of abdominal pain in the Emergency Department (ED). Common bile duct (CBD) identification is traditionally a standard component of the biliary ultrasound examination but can be challenging to perform for the novice sonographer. Previous work has demonstrated that CBD dilatation is rare in cases of cholecystitis with normal liver function tests (LFTs).

pmc-11454774.title: 7337 High Parathyroid Hormone (PTH) Due To Immunoassay Interference
pmc-11454774.creator: Vaidehi Alkeshbhai Mendpara, Adam J McShane, Leila Zeinab Khan
pmc-11454774.description: Disclosure: V.A. Mendpara: None. A.J. McShane: None. L.Z. Khan: None. Background: PTH levels are not always accurate. This case illustrates immunoassay interference in a female with markedly abnormal PTH values. Understanding immunoassay interference in diverse hormonal assessments can prevent diagnostic inaccuracies.

pmc-11692114.title: VESTA: A GROUNDBREAKING TOOL FOR ENHANCING FINANCIAL LITERACY AND SCAM RESILIENCE AMONG OLDER ADULTS
pmc-11692114.creator: Michael Barnett, Samuel Van Vleet, Rebekah Griffin, Matthew Fontanese, William Mallender, Harrison Boynton, Allyson Coldiron
pmc-11692114.description: VESTA (Virtual Economic Simulation and Trust Assessment) is a groundbreaking assessment tool designed to address the escalating challenges faced by older adults in the realm of modern financial capacity and digital literacy. VESTA replicates real-world scenarios in a smartphone setting to assess older adults’ ability to safely navigate virtual financial transactions, detect financial scams, and share information securely.

pmc-13065628.title: WALANT Thumb CMC Joint Denervation Under Field Sterility: A Case Report and Description of Technique
pmc-13065628.creator: Alexander Platt, Merry Faye Graff, Brett Ponich, Aaron Knox
pmc-13065628.description: Thumb carpometacarpal (CMC) osteoarthritis is a common condition that can affect a patient's ability to function normally in daily life. Surgical CMC denervation of the thumb has emerged as a less invasive option for patients who want to recover and return to activity sooner.

pmc-13340394.title: AI-assisted preoperative planning improves component sizing accuracy in Oxford unicompartmental knee arthroplasty: a retrospective cohort study with 24-month follow-up
pmc-13340394.creator: Fengrui Liu, Tong Li, Mengchen Yuan, Jiaxin Sun, Guoyuan Sun, Yaxing Duan, Zhengyuan Bai, Jinrui Sun, Xingyu Liu, Yiling Zhang, Qidong Zhang
pmc-13340394.description: BackgroundAccurate implant sizing is critical for clinical outcomes in Oxford unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA), yet reliable preoperative planning remains challenging. This study aimed to evaluate whether AI-assisted preoperative planning improves component sizing accuracy compared with conventional intraoperative instrumentation and to explore factors associated with component coverage.

pmc-13555343.title: Diminished general and sexual hedonic capacity in schizophrenia - a clinical and neural characterization
pmc-13555343.creator: S. Hamers, C. Sinke, N. Schultz, T.H.C. Krüger
pmc-13555343.description: BackgroundIndividuals with Schizophrenia are often reported to suffer from sexual dysfunction, but despite its clinical and individual relevance, the underlying neural mechanisms have not been investigated. To date it is unclear whether sexual problems are inherent to the disease, a secondary symptom, or a side effect of the antipsychotic agents.

pmc-13617630.title: Suspected Microplastic-Like Particles Recovered From Paired Human Small Intestine and Large Intestine Specimens: An Exploratory Post-mortem Study
pmc-13617630.creator: Eugen-Toma Radu, Nastaca Alina Palade, Crina Cristina Solomon, Manuela Pia Pumnea, Maria Totan, Claudia Maria Mihuț, Cecilia Georgescu, Claudiu Morgovan, Anca Butuca, Felicia Gabriela Gligor
pmc-13617630.description: BackgroundEvidence regarding suspected microplastic (MP)-like particles in human intestinal specimens remains limited. This study evaluated their occurrence and anatomical distribution in paired small and large intestinal specimens.MethodologyThis exploratory post-mortem study included 55 adults examined between March 2022 and December 2025. Intestinal specimens were processed using hydrogen peroxide digestion, glass-fiber filtration, Nile Red staining, fluorescence imaging, and ImageJ-based quantification.
